_note: English pronunciation drills by first language, for /kultur/fehler and the Aussprache-Check. Each drill practises one English sound or pattern that is hard from a particular first language (transfer, see fehler-nach-sprache.json). `pairs`: minimal pairs, the first word is the target, the second is what often comes out instead; both are real English words. `words`: practice words without a partner. `sentence`: to repeat, scored like the Aussprache-Check; it contains one word of every pair. `fehler`: the ids of the mistakes in fehler-nach-sprache.json that this drill practises (the other side of their `drill`; checked by pnpm check:aussprache). British English. Drill ids that still describe an English problem kept their slot id; th, w-v and ae are new (content-plan §5.6). Audio: scripts/generate-muttersprache-audio.mjs → public/audio/muttersprache/<slug>.mp3.

p-b.title: p or b?
p-b.tip: p comes with a small puff of air. Hold a piece of paper in front of your mouth: for p it moves, for b it doesn't.
p-b.sentence: Please pack a pear and a pin, then pull the door shut.

e-i-o-u.title: e or i · o or u?
e-i-o-u.tip: English has more vowels than many languages. pen and pin, lock and luck are different words. For e your mouth is a little more open than for i. For the o in lock your lips are round; for the u in luck they are relaxed.
e-i-o-u.sentence: Put the pen on the bed, then lock the door, but not the window.

sp-st.title: sp · st · sk at the start
sp-st.tip: No vowel before them and none between them: say “school”, not “eschool” or “ischool”. Start with the s straight away and go on to the next consonant.
sp-st.sentence: The student speaks Spanish at school.

ae.title: The a in cat
ae.tip: For /æ/, open your mouth wide and keep your tongue low and forward, a little like e. bad is not bed, cap is not cup.
ae.sentence: The man in the cap sat down. He had a bad day.

h.title: h at the start
h.tip: English h is only a soft breath, like breathing on a cold window. Don't leave it out, and don't make it rough in your throat.
h.sentence: Hold my hand. Can you hear the wind on the hill?

auslaut.title: b, d, g, z at the end
auslaut.tip: At the end of an English word, b, d, g, v and z keep their voice: bag is not back, prize is not price. Make the vowel before them a little longer.
auslaut.sentence: Put the prize in the bag, then feed the dog.

ende.title: Say the last consonant
ende.tip: Say the last sound so people can hear it. Without it, it's another word: bike is not buy, seat is not sea.
ende.sentence: My friend left his bike by the road and his card on the seat.

r-l.title: r or l?
r-l.tip: For l, touch the top of your mouth just behind your teeth with the tip of your tongue. For r, curl your tongue back a little and don't touch anything. right and light are different words.
r-l.sentence: Turn right on the main road and walk across the grass. Is that correct?

kurz-lang.title: Short i or long ee?
kurz-lang.tip: The i in ship is short and relaxed. The ee in sheep is long, and your lips are spread, as in a smile. The length changes the word: ship ≠ sheep, live ≠ leave.
kurz-lang.sentence: I live by the sea. It is lovely to sit and watch a ship go by.

w-v.title: w or v?
w-v.tip: For w, make your lips small and round, as for “oo”, then open them. Your teeth don't touch your lip. For v, your top teeth touch your bottom lip.
w-v.sentence: We drove west in the wet weather with a bottle of wine.

w-b.title: v or b?
w-b.tip: For v, your top teeth touch your bottom lip and you use your voice. For b, both lips close and open. van and ban, very and berry are different words.
w-b.sentence: Please vote for me: my very old van is the best.

betonung.title: Word stress
betonung.tip: Every English word with two or more syllables has one strong syllable, often the first: WAter, TEAcher, FAmily. Make it longer and louder; the other syllables are short and weak.
betonung.sentence: My teacher drinks a lot of water every morning.

th.title: th: think and this
th.tip: Put the tip of your tongue between your teeth. For think and three, push out only air. For they and this, use your voice too. Not s, t, f, d or z.
th.sentence: Thank you! I think they have three cats.

kein-e.title: No vowel at the end
kein-e.tip: Many English words end in a consonant. Stop on it: don't add a small “e” or “a”. big, not “bigga”; good, not “goode”.
kein-e.sentence: I've got a good job in a big shop.

s.title: z: the buzzing s
s.tip: z, and often s between vowels, buzzes like a bee: zoo, busy, music, easy. Use your voice: put your fingers on your throat and feel it shake.
s.sentence: Is the zoo busy on Tuesdays?

endkonsonanten.title: Consonants at the end
endkonsonanten.tip: Finish every word: let the last sound out. You can hear s, f and l at the end of English words: ice, life, school.
endkonsonanten.sentence: Life is nice in this place, but I don't like ice in my tea.

cluster.title: Consonants with no vowel between
cluster.tip: Some English words start with two or three consonants: str-, pl-, fr-, spr-. Say them straight after each other, with no vowel between them: “street”, not “sitreet”.
cluster.sentence: My friend plays on the street in spring.

verbendungen.title: The ending on the verb
verbendungen.tip: The ending tells you who and when: he works, she lives (-s); I worked, we played (-ed). Say it, even if it's only one small sound.
verbendungen.sentence: She works in a shop and lives near me. Yesterday she worked late.
